text:
maria: quick heads-up — saw a perf regression in continuous-batcher after the kernel swap. p95 up ~40% on kv-heavy traffic. attaching short profiler notes.

devin: can you paste the numbers/logs?

maria: p50 12ms -> 14ms, p95 80ms -> 112ms on the affected hosts. kv-hit rate ~62% for the sampled window. flame shows extra memcpy + strided kernel overhead.

raj: that sounds like the kernel chooser is favoring the strided/fused kernel based on seq len distribution, but it doesn't account for KV-hit localness. when KV hits are high we pay copy costs.

kai: fwiw queues got deeper during the window; admission started to pile up because per-token service time increased. would prefer softer backpressure earlier.

olivia: proposal: 1) add kv-hit ratio into kernel scoring; 2) run AB where we force a kv_friendly kernel hint + lower token budget for 10% traffic.

maria: agreed. quick experiment plan: roll 10% traffic -> kernel_hint=kv_friendly, token_budget_ms=10 (was 14), soft_limit_pct=0.8. measure p95, admissions.soft_429, avg_batch_fill.

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: rollout to canary (10%) in 2m, monitor window 2h, alert if p95 regress >5% or error rate >0.2%.

devin: add metrics: admissions_soft_429, avg_batch_fill_ratio, kv_hit_ratio to the dashboard. also trace kernel_decision reasons in the trace span.

raj: small config snippet for the canary: 

```
runtime.batch.hint = "kv_friendly"
runtime.batch.token_budget_ms = 10
runtime.batch.admit.soft_limit_pct = 0.80
runtime.batch.admit.hard_limit_pct = 0.95
metrics.export = ["admissions_soft_429","avg_batch_fill","kv_hit_ratio","kernel_choice_reason"]
```

olivia: link to the dashboard: <https://dash.redwood.internal/runtime/batcher/kv-admit-probe>?org=eng-runtime

maria: initial canary results: after 30m p95 stepped down to ~96ms for canary (vs 112ms baseline). admissions.soft_429 increased from 0 -> ~18/min on canary, avg_batch_fill dropped by ~6%. kv_hit_ratio stayed ~61%.

kai: tradeoff looks reasonable — fewer tail spikes at cost of slightly lower batch utilization. that matches our expectation.

devin: can we try a second AB where we keep token_budget=14 but tweak kernel scoring to prefer kv_friendly when kv_hit_ratio>0.5? might keep batch fill while avoiding memcpy overhead.

raj: i'll prototype kernel_score change: add a weight term w_kv * kv_hit_ratio to the score. default w_kv=0.6. will open PR with tests (unit + flame smoke).

maria: action items: maria -> PR to add canary config and dashboards; raj -> kernel scoring PR; kai -> monitor canary and flip thresholds if plateau; olivia -> add runbook blurb about soft-429 signals for support.

olivia: minor note: ensure the rollout has a short-circuit path to hard-reject if admissions.soft_429 > 100/min to avoid noisy cascading.

maria: good call. set an emergency guard on the config.

devin: cool. if kernel scoring + kv_hint combo still shows regressions we'll consider adaptive token budgets per route (route-level token_budget_ms).

maria: thanks team — will post PR links and the profiler capture in the channel once available. :thumbsup:
